basis: SCI-1 v1 evidence package: docs/sci1/SCI1_EVIDENCE_V1.md and src/data/scenarios/jezero-margin-unit.sci1-proposals.json
scope: Draft summaries of the SCI-1 v1 evidence, written by the AI agent and pending expert review.
They describe what an action could add relative to the Margin-unit work already done (three cores, three abrasions). They are not findings, and not predictions that the action would succeed.
Margin unit, Jezero crater. Sources: Mars 2020 Initial Reports Vol. 4 (Pelican Point and Comet Geyser reports) and NASA web pages retrieved on 2026-11-07.
Targets A–C are scenario positions with no verified geology.
Not used for scores, ranks or your plan.

observation.target: Whether distinctive sedimentary structures are present at Margin outcrops not yet examined.
observation.note: The reports name the missing structures as what keeps an igneous origin possible.
observation.instruments: Mastcam-Z zoom and 3D imaging; SuperCam chemistry and mineralogy from a distance.

unknowns.text: Only a positive result discriminates: absence of structures favours neither origin.
Whether structures would be visible: the western Margin already lacks clear sedimentary structures, and dusty, minimally layered surfaces may hide them.
Whether a suitable outcrop exists at Target A (a scenario position with no verified geology).

observation.target: Texture and fine-scale chemistry of a Margin rock not yet abraded; the source-named candidate is the lighter-toned, low-lying western Margin rock.
observation.note: None of the three existing abrasions is described as being on that rock.
observation.instruments: Abrasion, then WATSON close-up images, PIXL elemental chemistry and SHERLOC organics and altered minerals.

unknowns.text: Which abraded result would discriminate: none is source-supported yet. At Comet Geyser, texture and chemistry were each consistent with both sandstone and altered igneous rock. This is not evidence that abrasion lacks value.
What the lighter-toned rocks are, and whether they were abraded after sol 1088 (not established here).
Geology and accessibility at Target B (a scenario position).

observation.mode: Sealed sample · Earth laboratories, only if returned
observation.target: A core of a Margin rock the three existing cores do not represent; laboratories could test how its carbonate formed (detrital grains or in situ).
observation.note: Detrital carbonate would favour a sedimentary origin; in-situ carbonate alone would not decide the host rock's origin.
observation.instruments: Coring and sealing now; laboratory study only after return.

unknowns.text: Sample return: as retrieved on 2026-11-07, NASA's page describes Mars Sample Return in the past tense, as a proposed campaign.
What a fourth core adds: the three existing Margin cores are already proposed for the same laboratory questions.
Tube availability (not found) and geology at Target C (a scenario position).
